result.description: Open-source, customizable CRM (cloud or self-hosted) with custom objects, workflows and AI agents.
result.auth_detail: Workspace API key sent as Bearer token (Settings → Developers → API). OAuth2 auth-code + PKCE and client-credentials, with dynamic client registration (RFC 7591, POST /oauth/register), so no vendor app review.
result.access_detail: No app review or partner gate. OAuth clients self-register via RFC 7591, and API keys are per workspace. Cloud signup starts a 30-day trial, with paid plans at $9, $39 or $50k+ per year. REST/GraphQL API and MCP are listed as included on every plan, so there is no plan-based API restriction. The pricing page shows no permanent free cloud tier, so cloud access after the trial needs a paid plan. Self-hosting the open-source core is free, and that makes free self-serve possible for self-hosters. Rated trial rather than free because the hosted cloud, which most end users would connect, is trial then paid.
result.api_notes: Core API (/rest/, /graphql/) does CRUD on all records, including custom objects. Metadata API (/rest/metadata/, /metadata/) manages schema. Each workspace generates its own schema and docs. Batch operations take up to 60 records. Rate limit is 100 requests per minute. Webhooks are available.
result.blocker: No permanent free cloud tier (30-day trial, then paid). Multi-tenant hosts (workspace subdomains plus self-hosted domains) need a per-user base URL. Rate limit is 100 requests per minute. The schema differs per workspace.

evidence.quote: Create an API key in **Settings → Developers → API → + Create key**.
Twenty supports **dynamic client registration** per [RFC 7591](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591). No manual setup needed — register programmatically:
Sign up for Cloud in under a minute and start your 30-day trial.
Self-hosting the open source core is free.
Both are available as REST and GraphQL.

Twenty exposes an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server so that AI assistants — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, and others — can read and write your CRM data through natural language.
